texts: Performing a cavopulmonary anastomosis before 3 months of age is associated with increased hypoxia: B.
The SVC blood reaches the lungs only passively, so pulmonary vascular resistance must have fallen; in young infants it is still too high, and saturations drop.
Stage II is therefore usually done at 3 to 6 months; a bidirectional Glenn suits a later extracardiac conduit, and a hemi-Fontan sets up a lateral tunnel.
The hemi-Fontan is done on full bypass, often with a short period of arrest.
In the picture, before the third month the wooden blocks are still stacked and the baby's lips turn blue.
Memory hook: the astronaut waits for the third month.
